Five EU member states have announced plans to set up an offshore centre in Rwanda for people with no legal right to stay in Europe, in a pilot scheme that is expected to face legal challenges and has been denounced as “a grave moral failing”.
The five countries – Germany, Austria, the Netherlands, Denmark and Greece – are the first to seek to use the EU’s newly agreed returns law that allows people who have exhausted all avenues of appeal against their removal from Europe to be sent to a third country.

Demonstrators tried to block vehicle carrying the baboons, whose capture authorities say is needed to protect both primate and human
The relocation of a troop of baboons in Cape Town to a wildlife sanctuary has triggered furious protests by local people opposed to their capture, which officials argue is necessary to stop human-wildlife conflict in the city.
The 44-member Waterfall troop (named after the area they mainly inhabit) was captured in the southern seaside suburb of Simon’s Town on Friday and Saturday. A second, smaller Seaforth troop is also due to be moved.

Child reunited with family after he was detained by immigration agents in San Diego and transferred to Texas
An eight-year-old Haitian boy who was put into restraints and detained by immigration agents in San Diego on 4 November and transferred to a facility in Texas has been reunited with his family in California.
Representative Juan Vargas shared a photograph of the boy and his family in a social media post on Monda, writing: “11 days ago, an 8-year-old in San Diego was taken into federal custody during an immigration check-in. He was separated from his loved ones and held in a facility in Texas. Today, he’s finally home.”

The first known killing of a journalist ⁠in Costa Rica in ⁠25 years, ​Rodriguez’s death comes as the country grapples with a surge in drug violence driven by international trafficking groups, despite long ⁠being regarded as one of Central America’s most peaceful and stable democracies.

articles.title: European-made pesticides named in 1,605 poisoning reports in Brazil last year
articles.description:
About a third of cases involved chemicals banned for use on EU farms, according to investigation by Unearthed and Public Eye 
Pesticides sold by European chemical companies were named in more than 1,600 poisoning reports in Brazil last year, an investigation has found.
About a third of the cases involved chemicals banned from use on farms in the EU because of the risks they pose to people and the environment. But European companies are not banned from manufacturing these chemicals, as long as they export them overseas to countries where they are legally allowed to be used.

articles.title: New trade-restrictive measures surge but WTO members step up trade facilitation efforts
articles.description: The pace of newly-introduced tariffs and other non-facilitating measures rose sharply in the first half of 2026, while the stockpile of such measures reached a record level, according to the WTO Director-General's latest annual overview of developments in the international trading environment. At the same time, WTO members introduced a significant number of trade-facilitating measures, helping to sustain global trade flows despite heightened geopolitical tensions and economic uncertainty.
articles.titleJa: 貿易制限措置が急増する一方、WTO加盟国は貿易円滑化の取り組みを強化

articles.title: Ireland contributes EUR 200,000 to strengthen trade opportunities in developing countries
articles.description: Ireland is contributing EUR 200,000 (approximately CHF 185,000) to the Standards and Trade Development Facility (STDF) in 2026 to strengthen sanitary and phytosanitary capacity in developing and least-developed countries. The contribution will support STDF activities that help countries meet international food safety and animal and plant health standards, as well as facilitate safe and inclusive trade.
articles.titleJa: アイルランド、途上国の貿易機会強化に20万ユーロを拠出

articles.title: South Africa notifies launch of safeguard investigation into certain non-wired float glass products

articles.title: Ethiopia's accession maintains momentum as WTO members review progress
articles.description: At its eighth meeting on 9 and 10 November, the Working Party on Ethiopia's Accession to the WTO took stock of the latest progress in bilateral market access negotiations and reforms of Ethiopia's foreign trade regime. Leading a high-level delegation, Ethiopia's Minister of Trade and Regional Integration and Chief Trade Negotiator, Yasmin Wohabrebbi Saeed, reaffirmed the priority the government continues to attach to achieving WTO accession as soon as possible. Members welcomed the progress achieved while noting that further work is needed before the accession process can be concluded.
articles.titleJa: エチオピアのWTO加盟、進捗状況の確認で勢いを維持

articles.title: Germany contributes EUR 500,000 to strengthen developing economies' trade capacity
articles.description: Germany is contributing EUR 500,000 (approximately CHF 460,000) to the WTO's Global Trust Fund (GTF) to help developing economies and least developed countries (LDCs) enhance their participation in the multilateral trading system. Carmen Heidecke, Ambassador of Germany to the WTO, signed the Memorandum of Understanding on behalf of the German Federal Government at the WTO headquarters in Geneva on 9 November 2026.
articles.titleJa: ドイツ、途上国の貿易能力強化に50万ユーロを拠出

articles.title: EU launches safeguard investigation on certain PET resin chemicals

articles.title: Director-General: Leverage trade and partnerships to build a resilient ocean economy
articles.description: The multilateral trading system provides important tools for the development of a healthy and prosperous ocean economy, Director-General Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala said in her keynote speech at an event on Trade, Biodiversity and the Ocean Economy: Pathways to Resilience at the WTO on 5 November. Highlighting the importance of strengthening support for coastal and island economies, she said: Trade is part of the answer. The oceans are an asset of the global commons that can best be managed through multilateral approaches. The event was co-organized by Belgium, Fiji and Portugal.
articles.titleJa: 事務局長：貿易とパートナーシップを活用し、強靭な海洋経済を構築

articles.title: Members review progress in resolving SPS trade concerns at WTO
articles.description: The WTO's Committee on Sanitary and Phytosanitary (SPS) Measures met on 4-6 November, receiving an update on the resolution of past SPS-related trade concerns raised by members, reviewing a list of new and previously raised trade concerns, and advancing work on transparency, mentoring and technical cooperation issues.
